title: Why Do We Hiccup?
description:
Why Do We Hiccup?
A Pip and Ray science short. Educational, not medical advice.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Hic! Hic! Oh no. RAY! I have the hiccups... and they will NOT stop!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Relax, Pip. It is just your diaphragm throwing a tiny tantrum.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: My dia-WHAT? Is that a muscle or a dinosaur?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: It is the big breathing muscle under your lungs. And sometimes... it suddenly squeezes all on its own.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: But WHY? Did I offend it somehow?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: You probably triggered it yourself. Eating too fast, fizzy drinks, even getting excited can irritate the nerves that run it.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Nerves?! My belly is bossed around by NERVES?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: By the vagus and phrenic nerves, yes. They tell the diaphragm when to move. Irritate them... and it spasms.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Okay, but that squeaky HIC... where does the sound come from?

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: The instant your diaphragm yanks air in, a little gate in your throat, the glottis, slams shut. That slam... is the hic.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: A slamming gate in my throat. Incredible. Hic!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: And here is the weird part: nobody knows for sure WHY we hiccup. One theory says it is a leftover reflex from ancient ancestors who breathed through gills.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: You are telling me I have FISH technology in my chest?! Hic!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Maybe! Hiccups usually fade on their own. Sip some water slowly... and let the reflex calm down.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Fine. I will out-wait my own throat. SCIENCE!
